findings.title: PHP core remote code execution (PHP2Shell)
findings.description: Memory-handling flaws in the PHP runtime. On Apache with mod_php an unauthenticated request could trigger code execution before application code ran; PHP-FPM was also confirmed exploitable through application code paths. Fixing application code or plugins does not fix it: the PHP binary must be updated.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (or a distro package that backports the fix).
remediation: Upgrade PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (or a distro package that backports the fix).
Rebuild and redeploy Docker images (docker build --pull).
PHP 8.1 and older have no regular upstream fix: plan the upgrade.
A WAF rule is defense in depth, not a fix.

findings.title: Firebase rules allow public access
findings.description: Anyone with your public Firebase config can read or write this data.
findings.recommendation: Require request.auth and check ownership in the rules.

findings.title: next 16.3.0: Next.js unauthenticated RCE (use cache typed arrays, Image Optimization SVG) and Server Actions DoS
findings.description: Two critical unauthenticated remote code execution issues (App Router 'use cache' functions returning typed arrays; Image Optimization API with SVG on glibc Linux) and a high-severity Server Actions denial of service.
remediation: npm install next@16.4.1 (16.x) or next@15.5.28 (15.x).
Make sure the resolved sharp version is 0.35.5 or later.
Redeploy after upgrading.

findings.title: Laravel APP_DEBUG=true with APP_ENV=production
findings.description: Debug pages show stack traces, environment variables and queries to anyone who triggers an error.

findings.title: AWS access key ID in source
findings.description: A credential appears to be stored in the repository. Anyone with access to the code, its history, a leaked build or the browser bundle can use it.
findings.recommendation: Revoke/rotate the credential first, then move it to environment variables or a secrets manager.
remediation: Rotate the key in the provider dashboard (assume it is compromised).
Load it from an environment variable / secrets manager.
Remove it from git history (git filter-repo) if the repository was ever shared.
Add a pre-commit secret scanner.

findings.title: Stripe live secret/restricted key in source
findings.description: A credential appears to be stored in the repository. Anyone with access to the code, its history, a leaked build or the browser bundle can use it.
findings.recommendation: Revoke/rotate the credential first, then move it to environment variables or a secrets manager.
remediation: Rotate the key in the provider dashboard (assume it is compromised).
Load it from an environment variable / secrets manager.
Remove it from git history (git filter-repo) if the repository was ever shared.
Add a pre-commit secret scanner.

findings.title: Untrusted event data interpolated into a shell step
findings.description: Titles, bodies and branch names are attacker-controlled; ${{ }} is substituted before the shell runs, so they can inject commands.
findings.recommendation: Pass the value through env: and reference it as "$VAR".

findings.title: Shell command built from a template or concatenation
findings.description: child_process.exec runs the string through a shell. Interpolating variables lets an attacker append extra commands with characters like ; | && or $().
findings.recommendation: Use execFile/spawn with an argument array and no shell, and validate inputs against an allow-list.
remediation: Switch to execFile(cmd, [arg1, arg2]) or spawn(cmd, args, { shell: false }).
Validate every argument with an allow-list (e.g. /^[a-z0-9-]+$/).
Never pass request data straight to a shell.

findings.title: Server Actions accept any origin
findings.description: allowedOrigins with '*' disables the origin check that protects Server Actions from CSRF.

findings.title: SQL query built with PHP variables
findings.description: Concatenating or interpolating variables into SQL lets attackers rewrite the query.
findings.recommendation: Use prepared statements (PDO/mysqli) or Eloquent/Query Builder bindings.
remediation: $stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?'); $stmt->execute([$id]);
In Laravel: DB::select('... where id = ?', [$id]) or ->whereRaw('id = ?', [$id]).
Cast numeric inputs with (int).

findings.title: .env is not covered by .gitignore
findings.description: No .gitignore rule matches this env file, so it can be committed by accident.
findings.recommendation: Add .env* to .gitignore and keep a .env.example without values.

findings.title: Django DEBUG = True
findings.description: Debug pages leak settings and code if this file is used in production.
findings.recommendation: Read DEBUG from the environment and default to False.

findings.title: ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*']
findings.description: Any Host header is accepted, enabling host-header poisoning of password-reset links.

findings.title: Database port published on all interfaces
findings.description: The database is reachable from outside the host if the firewall allows it.
findings.recommendation: Remove the ports mapping or bind it to 127.0.0.1.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.description: If the app is compromised, the attacker is root inside the container, which makes escapes and lateral movement easier.
findings.recommendation: Add a non-root USER in the final stage.
remediation: RUN adduser -D app (or useradd) and USER app
Official node images ship a 'node' user: USER node

findings.title: Express app without helmet
findings.description: helmet sets sensible security headers (CSP, HSTS, noSniff, frameguard) in one line.

findings.title: No security headers configured for Next.js
findings.description: No Content-Security-Policy, HSTS or frame protection was found in next.config, vercel.json or middleware. Headers limit the impact of XSS and clickjacking.
findings.recommendation: Add headers() in next.config with CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and frame-ancestors.
remediation: async headers() { return [{ source: '/(.*)', headers: [...] }] }
Verify on the live site with: nfaudit headers https://your-site

findings.title: X-Powered-By header not disabled
findings.description: Next.js announces itself in X-Powered-By. It does not create a vulnerability but helps fingerprinting.

notes: Dependencies were only checked against the small built-in advisory list. Run with --osv (sends package names and versions to OSV.dev, never code) for full CVE coverage.
